flashcard_questions.q: What are weapons of mass destruction?
flashcard_questions.a: Weapons that kill huge numbers of people over a wide area.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of weapon of mass destruction uses disease?
Which type of weapon of mass destruction uses poisonous substances?
How many people were killed by the atomic bombs of 1945?
What is nuclear deterrence in modern warfare?
flashcard_questions.a: Keeping nuclear weapons so that no nation risks attacking.

flashcard_questions.q: Which Cold War strategy is abbreviated to MAD?
Why do nuclear weapons break the just war rule on proportionality?
flashcard_questions.a: Their destructive power is far too great to be proportionate.

flashcard_questions.q: What did Pope Francis say about even possessing nuclear weapons?
What does the Qur’an 16:126 require of a response to attack?
What argument do supporters of nuclear deterrence make?
flashcard_questions.a: Nuclear weapons have prevented major wars between nuclear powers since 1945.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main moral objection to nuclear deterrence?
flashcard_questions.a: It relies on a willingness to kill millions of innocent civilians.

flashcard_questions.q: Which archbishop led the peaceful fight against apartheid in South Africa?
Why did Malala Yousafzai become the youngest-ever Nobel Peace Prize laureate?
flashcard_questions.a: She campaigned for girls’ right to education despite Taliban death threats.

flashcard_questions.q: Where was Islamic Relief Worldwide founded?
Which Islamic principle inspires the work of Islamic Relief Worldwide?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term→definition (WMDs, biological, chemical, deterrence), 3 argument→view (deterrence for, deterrence against, proportionality), 3 denomination→position (Pope Francis, Qur’an 16:126, MAD), 3 person/organisation (Tutu, Malala, Islamic Relief), 2 case-study facts.
